task: [.github/workflows/improvement-bot.yml] .github/workflows/improvement-bot.yml iş akışındaki 72 saniyelik medyan çalışma süresini optimize etmek için Pip ve apt paket adımlarına `actions/cache` entegre edilerek bağımlılıkların tekrar indirilmesi önlenmeli, workflow tetikleme kurallarına `paths` filtreleri (ör. kaynak kod dışındaki dokümantasyon güncellemelerini atlamak için) eklenmeli ve birbirine bağımlı olmayan test adımları müstakil paralel job'lara bölünerek eşzamanlı yürütülmelidir.

evidence.detail: Target workflow file requiring optimization to reduce the 72-second median runtime via dependency caching, trigger path filters, and job parallelization.

factual_findings: .github/workflows/improvement-bot.yml currently executes steps sequentially without dependency caching for Pip or apt packages.
Workflow triggers in .github/workflows/improvement-bot.yml lack path filters, causing execution on changes that do not affect runtime code (e.g., documentation changes).
Independent test steps are bounded within a single job rather than executing concurrently across parallel jobs.
hypotheses: Integrating actions/cache or setup-python built-in caching for Pip dependencies in .github/workflows/improvement-bot.yml will avoid redundant dependency downloads.
Adding 'paths' or 'paths-ignore' filters (e.g., ignoring '**.md' or 'docs/**') to workflow triggers will skip unnecessary runs on non-code updates.
Splitting independent test steps into separate parallel jobs in .github/workflows/improvement-bot.yml will lower total workflow duration below the 72-second median baseline.
result.recommendation: Refactor .github/workflows/improvement-bot.yml by adding 'paths-ignore' filters to triggers, configuring Pip dependency caching, and matrixing/splitting independent test steps into concurrent jobs.
result.next_action: Modify .github/workflows/improvement-bot.yml with the caching, path filter, and parallel job structure, then verify workflow execution performance.
